protocol.name: qdwin_nested_v1
protocol.copyright: qdistro-internal protocol. Not for external use.
protocol.description:
Protocol by which a **nested** Wayland compositor running inside qdwin advertises its inner toplevels as peer surfaces in the outer qdwin. Enables multi-window containerised apps (tier-2 isolation per `the architecture doc` + `the architecture doc`) to surface as native-feeling toplevels in the admin shell instead of a single "window-of-windows."
Design decision (§6.8 S0, 2026-04-25): Shape-A (per-toplevel PipeWire streams piped from nested weston into outer qdwin proxy surfaces) rather than Shape-B (Wayland re-marshalling bridge). Rationale:
- §6.5 already ships per-view PipeWire streams; re-using the pipeline avoids a second bespoke transport. - Shape-B (Wayland re-marshal) requires the bridge to parse and translate every Wayland request, including wl_buffer, wl_shm, and backend-specific buffer types; multi-month implementation cost. - Shape-A keeps the nested compositor a black box; any inner surface that renders onto its output is capturable, including apps using any Wayland extension the inner compositor speaks.
Relationship to xdg-foreign: xdg-foreign is intentionally scoped to client-to-client bridging inside one wl_display. It does not span a nested → outer boundary because the inner wl_surface isn't accessible from the outer compositor in any form. qdwin_nested_v1 fills that gap.
Lifecycle:
1. Nested weston binds wp_qdwin_nested_manager_v1. 2. For each new inner toplevel, nested weston captures it to a PipeWire node (backend-pipewire, per-view), captures its input sink (for keyboard/pointer injection), and calls advertise_toplevel(pw_node, input_sink, app_id, title, origin_uid). 3. Outer qdwin creates a proxy wl_surface, attaches a buffer fed by the PipeWire source, sends toplevel_added on qdwin_shell_v1 so qdshell decorates it like any other toplevel. 4. Inner toplevel destruction → nested weston destroys the corresponding qdwin_nested_toplevel_v1 resource; outer qdwin tears down the proxy surface.
Authorisation:
The manager global is hidden from generic secctx/silo clients. The launcher-minted `qdistro.tier2` `/usr/bin/weston` publisher is the sole secctx exception, repeated at bind time; all binders are also peer-uid-filtered. Advertised inner toplevels are capped per uid before allocation. The outer-qdwin-side policy decision for "is this nested compositor allowed to publish each of its inner toplevels" lives in the admin broker (`qdistro.nested.advertise:<app_id>`); qdwin holds proxies invisible/input-empty until the shell reports that decision. If no v8+ shell can broker the request, production/default config keeps the proxy held fail-closed.

interface.name: qdwin_nested_manager_v1

description.summary: bind entry point for nested compositor passthrough

interface.description: Obtained via wl_registry.bind by the nested compositor. Hidden from generic secctx clients by the global filter, with an exact `qdistro.tier2` + `/usr/bin/weston` exception for the production nested publisher. The bind handler repeats that identity check and applies the peer-uid filter.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager does not tear down already-advertised toplevels; each qdwin_nested_toplevel_v1 must be destroyed explicitly.

request.name: advertise_toplevel

description.summary: publish a new inner toplevel to outer qdwin

request.description:
The nested compositor has already arranged a PipeWire source node (pw_node) carrying the toplevel pixels and an input sink (input_sink) that accepts synthesised pointer/keyboard events which the nested compositor forwards to the corresponding inner client. Both node IDs use PipeWire's global serial as opaque identifiers — outer qdwin resolves them via the PipeWire registry on its own session.
origin_uid is the uid owning the inner client (for per-uid colour chip + broker authz). app_id and title follow the standard xdg_toplevel semantics.
On successful advertise the outer qdwin sends the initial `configured` event with the size picked by the admin shell; before that event fires the inner client should not yet be allowed to interact (implementation detail left to the nested compositor).

arg.name: pw_node
arg.summary: PipeWire source-node identifier (v2: string of form 'weston.pipewire:<nested-pid>:<weston-output-name>' or, for protocol-debug, an empty string meaning 'no pixels yet — placeholder advertise'). Outer side resolves to a global serial via libpipewire on its own session bus.

arg.name: input_sink
arg.summary:
Input-sink identifier for input injection. Format (S3 onward): a unix socket path of the form `/run/user/<uid>/qdwin-nested-input-<pid>-<hndl>.sock` that the nested compositor listens on. The outer side connects to it and writes binary packets:
offset size field 0 4 magic = 0x49444E51 ('QDNI', LE) 4 1 version (1) 5 1 event_type (1 PING, 2 motion, 3 button, 4 key, 5 axis, 6 focus) 6 2 payload_len 8 … payload (per event_type)
S3 ships only event_type=1 PING — proves the wire + roundtrip. S3b adds the real motion/button/key encoders. Empty string means 'no input sink' (S1 backward-compat; outer treats the proxy as display-only).

entry.name: bad_pw_node
entry.summary: pw_node doesn't resolve on outer's PipeWire

entry.name: duplicate
entry.summary: pw_node already advertised by this manager

interface.name: qdwin_nested_toplevel_v1

description.summary: one nested inner toplevel, surfaced as outer peer

interface.description: Handle on an advertised inner toplevel. Lifetime is bounded by the nested compositor; the outer qdwin only observes.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The nested compositor sends this when its inner toplevel is destroyed (client exit, map→unmap, etc.). The outer qdwin tears down the proxy surface and removes the toplevel from qdwin_shell_v1.toplevel_added tracking.

request.name: set_geometry
request.description: Suggested inner content size (not including outer chrome). Outer qdwin may clamp or round to its own tiling rules.

event.name: configured

description.summary: outer qdwin has picked a size for the toplevel

event.description: Fired once after a successful advertise_toplevel and any time the outer shell changes the allocated size. Nested compositor should reconfigure its inner client accordingly.

event.name: close_requested

description.summary: admin shell asked for the toplevel to close

event.description: Fired when the user clicks the outer close glyph or the admin shell issues qdwin_shell_v1.request_close for this proxy surface. Nested compositor propagates to its inner client via xdg_toplevel.close (or its private equivalent).

event.name: focus_changed

request.name: set_remote_identity
request.description: Available only to the root-installed remote viewer helper. The compositor verifies the publishing process executable independently and accepts this immutable tuple once. Ordinary nested publishers cannot cause qdwin to mark a proxy as remotely authenticated.
